newsitem.title: COMOROS: French firemen cut 27 bodies from Ethiopia plane.
newsitem.headline: French firemen cut 27 bodies from Ethiopia plane.

text.p: French firemen using newly-delivered cutting equipment recovered 27 bodies from the wreck of a hijacked Ethiopian Airlines plane that crashed in the sea off the Comoro Islands, officials said on Tuesday.
The firemen pulled 21 bodies from the mid-section of the fuselage of the Boeing 767 on Monday after the wreckage was dragged on to a beach 40 km (25 miles) north of the Comoro capital Moroni.
Six more bodies from the cockpit which was submerged several hundred metres (yards) out to sea were also recovered, said Captain Bruno Beausse, head of the 25-strong team of French firemen.
The team from the Indian Ocean island of Reunion included 12 divers.
New equipment for the firemen arrived from Reunion on Monday and scaffolding was used to prop up the fuselage.

"We have cleared the right part of the fuselage, but we were worried that if we cleared the left part the fuselage could fall down from the scaffolding so we stopped work tonight," Beausse told Reuters.
Work would resume at low tide on Tuesday morning and the crew expected to recover the remaining six bodies from the fuselage and a further six or seven from the cockpit area, he said.
That would leave less than 10 bodies in the plane that crashed into the sea some 500 metres (yards) from the Comoro coast on Saturday after it apparently ran out of fuel.
In Addis Ababa, Ethiopian Airlines officials said the presumed death toll had risen to 125 after two people who survived the crash died of their injuries.
The plane was hijacked by three men, believed to be Ethiopians, when it was en route to Nairobi and West Africa from the Ethiopian capital.
Fifty of the 175 passengers and crew, including two of the suspected hijackers, are now believed to have survived.
Ethiopian Airlines made preparations on Monday to take survivors back to Addis Ababa.
Senior Comoron government officials said Ethiopia had requested the extradition of the two suspected hijackers.

"To my knowledge no decision has been taken about releasing the suspects, but we have received an extradition request from the Ethiopian government," Secretary of State (Minister) for Information Assoumani Youssouf told Reuters.
He was responding to rumours the two men might be released on grounds they had been wrongly identified.
"This is a criminal affair and an inquiry is under way. The two suspects have not been charged and it will be up to the judiciary to take any decisions," said gendarmerie commander Ismael Mognidayo.
Of the 163 passengers and 12 crew on board the plane, 145 were international travellers from some 35 countries and 30 were Ethiopians.
